record.paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
record.original_question: Do there exist real numbers α and β such that for every ε>0, liminf_{q→∞} q(log q)^{2−ε}⟨qα⟩⟨qβ⟩ is positive?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 37 (A. Pollington). Are there α, β ∈ R such that for every ε > 0, lim infq→∞ q(log q)2− ε 〈qα〉 〈qβ〉> 0?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a real number $x$, let $\langle x\rangle$ denote the distance from $x$ to the nearest integer. Do there exist real numbers $\alpha$ and $\beta$ such that for every $\varepsilon > 0$,
$$\liminf_{q\to\infty}\, q\,(\log q)^{2-\varepsilon}\,\langle q\alpha\rangle\,\langle q\beta\rangle \;>\; 0\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: The question concerns a logarithmically strengthened version of Littlewood's conjecture: whether there exist α, β with q(log q)^{2-ε} ⟨qα⟩⟨qβ⟩ bounded below. Gallagher's theorem shows the set of such pairs has Lebesgue measure zero, but no explicit pair is known. Recent surveys on Littlewood's conjecture (Bugeaud–Moshchevitin, Beresnevich–Velani, Badziahin–Pollington–Velani) discuss this and related strengthenings as open problems; no construction or disproof appears in the literature.

status_evidence.title: On some open problems in Diophantine approximation
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Mad_λ = {(α,β) : liminf q(log q)^λ ||qα|| ||qβ|| > 0} and notes the set has Lebesgue measure zero for λ ≤ 2.
status_evidence.claim: Strengthened Littlewood-type problems of this form are surveyed as open.

status_evidence.title: Metrical musings on Littlewood and friends
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Gallagher-type strengthening of Littlewood with logarithmic factors and known measure-theoretic results.
status_evidence.claim: No explicit pair (α,β) with the logarithmic strengthening is known.
